source: NHS England PRN02356 - Quality and Outcomes Framework guidance for 2026/27 (effective 1 April 2026). Underpinned by NICE indicator menu IDs where shown in indicator notes. NOTE (qof-007, 2026-07-25): a July 2026 amendment document exists (PRN02356-quality-outcomes-framework-guidance-2026-27-july-update.pdf); content not readable this run (403) — next Keeper run should check all indicators against the amendment. DEM004 is the only indicator confirmed to have been wrong (now corrected in this run).
notes: 2026-09-05: qof-reg-obes2 added (OBES2_REG / TA1026 cohort) and qof-ob005 rewritten to PCIT pathway codes — see those rules' notes. Register membership uses substring matching on problem labels (approximation of QOF SNOMED refsets). Indicator checks use the most recent matching observation within the indicator window. Frailty exclusion is implemented via excludeIfProblem on each affected indicator. Retired 25/26 indicators are kept disabled to make the year-on-year diff visible. This is a memory aid only; not for QOF claim purposes. 2026-06-04 (The Keeper): added the NEW 26/27 Obesity clinical area — OB register (enabled, BMI-driven so substring-approximated) plus indicators OB004/OB005 shipped DISABLED as drafts pending CSO confirmation of points/thresholds against PRN02356. 2026-06-10: enabled HF009 (medication-all-of engine support added) and DM037 (observation-bundle already supported). 2026-07-11 (The Keeper): added LD register; DEM004 (dementia care plan review); CKD002 (BP target) and CKD003 (ACEi/ARB in CKD+HYP+proteinuria); CHOL003 extended to PAD, STIA, CKD registers (3 new clones); CHOL004 extended to PAD and STIA registers (2 new clones; CKD explicitly NOT covered by CHOL004 per PRN02356). Primary PDF 403 that run — all corroborated via PRN02356 search. 2026-07-25 (The Keeper): CORRECTED DEM004 (30pts/60-90% → 14pts/35-70% — was wrong due to 403 on primary PDF); ENABLED OB register with ageMin:18 corrected (was 16, wrong for QOF 2026/27 definition); LD notes updated to clarify DES/enhanced-service status of annual health check; AF006 upper:95 CONFIRMED correct for 26/27 (proposed revert to 90% killed by VERIFIER-B). PRN02356 July 2026 amendment noted above. 2026-08-22 (The Keeper): added the rest of the SMI physical-health suite alongside MH011 — MH002 (care plan, 5pts 40-90%), MH003 (BP, 3pts), MH006 (BMI, 3pts), MH007 (alcohol, 3pts), MH012 (glucose/HbA1c, 7pts; diabetes excluded via excludeIfProblem, never bare 'diabetes') — all observation-recent on the SMI register, flat 12-month windows, verified against PRN02356 July 2026 update + NICE IND143/IND84/IND83/IND82/IND159. 2026-08-27: added medicusRegisterTypes to DM/DEM/HYP/AF/CHD/COPD/OB — Medicus's own clinical-summary endpoint returns a `patientRegisters` array with its own computed register membership (verified via a real HAR capture, test patient 01923625-8042-7071-a04d-1c610de03944), which the engine now prefers over problem-text-matching for these 7 registers when available (see patientOnRegister in rules-engine.js) — it is not subject to the stray 'family history of X' false-positive that text-matching can hit. Only these 7 registerType strings have been confirmed against real data; ASTHMA (and the remaining STIA/CKD/PAD/SMI/LD/HF registers) still use text-matching only until a HAR from a patient genuinely on each of those registers confirms the real registerType string — do not guess unconfirmed strings (same silent-failure caution as drug-rules.json match lists). 2026-08-27 follow-up: HAR from a genuine asthma-register patient (test patient 019235dd-c0e3-7234-85c9-931844b47691) confirmed registerType 'medicus-health/register-asthma' (note the register-X prefix, matching AF's pattern, not the -register suffix most others use) — added to ASTHMA. STIA/CKD/PAD/SMI/LD/HF remain unconfirmed.

rules.source: QOF 26/27 AST register. Underlying business rules amended for 26/27 to include patients from age 5 (was 6); Sentinel's substring match is age-agnostic so this change has no functional effect here. 2026-08-27: added family history / suspected / query exclusions (matching the LD register's precedent) — a stray "Family history of asthma" or "?asthma" problem was otherwise counting as register membership and, worse, could supply a spuriously old codedDate that blocked AST012 from firing for a genuinely new diagnosis coded later.
QOF 26/27 COPD register. Underlying business rules amended for 26/27 to address potential under/over-recording; the SNOMED refset has been refined but Sentinel's substring match is unchanged.
QOF 26/27 MH register (SMI_COD refset approximation — schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, other psychoses)

QOF 26/27 OB register (NHS England PRN02356). ENABLED 2026-07-25 (The Keeper, qof-003 AMBER): register is active in QOF 2026/27. ageMin corrected from 16 to 18 simultaneously — the QOF register definition specifies adults aged 18+ (BMI ≥30, or ≥27.5 for South Asian, Chinese, other Asian, Middle Eastern, Black African or African-Caribbean patients). VERIFIER-B confirmed at HIGH confidence from multiple NHS England QOF 2026/27 sources. CSO should review before first QOF claim.
rules.notes: NEW for 26/27. The true QOF Obesity register is BMI-driven (adults aged 18+ with a BMI ≥30, or ≥27.5 for people of South Asian, Chinese, other Asian, Middle Eastern, Black African or African-Caribbean family background, recorded in the preceding 12 months) — it is NOT a problem-coded register. Sentinel approximates it here with substring problem-matching (ageMin:18 enforced to match QOF definition — 16-17 year olds are correctly excluded), which will MISS obese patients who have a recorded BMI but no 'obesity' problem label. Proper membership needs a BMI-observation-based register (engine extension) before this can be fully relied on. OB004 still uses this general register. OB005 does NOT — it uses qof-reg-obes2 (OBES2_REG / TA1026 cohort).

rules.source: PCIT OB005 / QOF 26/27 OBES2_REG (NICE TA1026 funding-variation cohort). Distinct from the general QOF obesity register (BMI ≥30 / ≥27.5).
rules.notes: Engine-evaluated BMI + 4-of-5 comorbidity cohort. Ethnicity unknown uses the 35 kg/m² threshold (cannot apply the 32.5 adjustment without evidence). Dyslipidaemia is statin OR latest LDL/TG/HDL thresholds, not a problem label. Hypertension and T2DM are dropped when a resolved code is present and not followed by a later active code. This is a memory aid, not a QOF claim tool — SNOMED refset membership remains an approximation via substring / listed codes.

rules.source: QOF 26/27 LD register (LD_COD refset approximation — corroborated via PRN02356 search; primary PDF 403 this run). Added 2026-07-11 (The Keeper). 2026-07-25 (qof-006, VERIFIER-B GREEN): LD annual health check confirmed as a Directed Enhanced Service (DES), NOT a core QOF clinical indicator — notes updated accordingly.
rules.notes: The QOF LD register is defined by SNOMED codes for intellectual disability; Sentinel approximates via problem substring matching. This will miss patients with a learning disability not coded using these terms. Down's syndrome and Fragile X are the most commonly encountered specific diagnoses in primary care LD registers. Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) without intellectual disability does NOT qualify for the QOF LD register — autistic patients who do not have a separately coded intellectual disability are correctly not flagged. LD ANNUAL HEALTH CHECK: confirmed as a Directed Enhanced Service (DES/Learning Disability Health Check Scheme 2025-2028, managed via CQRS), NOT a core QOF clinical domain indicator — the QOF LD register identifies eligible patients but the health check itself and its £140 payment sit in enhanced services. Health check indicator (LD004-equivalent) not encoded here; the DES-linked check should be tracked separately via the enhanced-services workflow.

rules.source: QOF 26/27 NDH register (NHS England PRN02356 — NDH003 'Reporting and verification': "the register... is defined as all patients aged 18 or over with a record of non-diabetic hyperglycaemia or pre-diabetes or GDM, which has not been superseded by a diagnosis of diabetes (excluding GDM) recorded prior to the beginning of the financial year"). Fetched and confirmed in full 2026-08-28 (The Keeper) — https://www.england.nhs.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/prn02356-quality-outcomes-framework-guidance-2026-27-july-update.pdf pp.57-58. NEW to Sentinel this run — was held pending confirmation (see qof-ndh in .claude/skills/the-keeper/references/state/last-run.json), now resolved and applied.
rules.notes: problemExclude deliberately uses "type 1 diabetes"/"type 2 diabetes" rather than bare "diabetes mellitus" — a bare "diabetes mellitus" exclude would also match "Gestational diabetes mellitus" as a substring and wrongly drop the very GDM patients this register must include (the QOF definition explicitly excludes progression to diabetes but excludes GDM from that exclusion). Known approximation: a patient coded with bare "Diabetes mellitus" (no type specified) who has progressed from NDH will not be excluded — same class of imprecision the DM register itself accepts elsewhere in this file. ageMin:18 per the QOF register definition ("aged 18 or over") — enforced at evaluate time via registerAgeRange (fail-open when age is unknown).

rules.indicatorName: HbA1c or fasting glucose recorded in NDH/prior GDM (preceding 12 months)
rules.source: QOF 26/27 NDH003 (NICE IND172/IND173) — NHS England PRN02356: "The percentage of patients with non-diabetic hyperglycaemia or a previous diagnosis of gestational diabetes who have had an HbA1c or fasting blood glucose performed in the preceding 12 months." 20pts, 50-90%. Fetched and confirmed in full 2026-08-28 (The Keeper) — https://www.england.nhs.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/prn02356-quality-outcomes-framework-guidance-2026-27-july-update.pdf pp.57-58. rules.notes: Frailty-stratified replacement for DM008. Fires ONLY for patients on the DM register WITH moderate OR severe frailty coded — expressed via requiresAnyProblem (disjunctive: any one of the listed frailty levels). The engine now honours requiresAnyProblem (negation-aware), so this no longer over-triggers for all DM patients.

rules.indicatorName: Statin primary prevention in DM >=40 (no CVD, no frailty)

rules.indicatorName: Statin secondary prevention in DM with CVD history
rules.notes: Secondary prevention. Uses requiresAnyProblem — fires only if a DM register patient has at least one CVD problem coded (negation-aware, so 'family history of stroke' does not qualify). Excludes haemorrhagic stroke. The rules engine now honours requiresAnyProblem.

rules.notes: NEW 26/27 indicator. Replaces HF003 and HF006. Requires concurrent prescription from all 4 drug classes in HFrEF. Clinician must verify: contraindication and intolerance exclusions are NOT detectable from coded records; a patient shown as not_met may have documented reasons for omitting one or more pillars. 2026-06-17 (The Keeper, CSO-approved): RAAS pillar brought to parity with the file's ACE/ARB list — added fosinopril, olmesartan and azilsartan, so a HFrEF patient whose sole RAAS agent is one of those no longer silently fails the RAAS pillar.

rules.indicatorName: Asthma review with 4 components in preceding 12 months
rules.source: QOF 26/27 AST015 (PRN02356 July 2026 update, changelog table: "AST015 Changed indicator ID due to asthma register change", thresholds/points unchanged from prior AST007)
rules.notes: 2026-08-28 (The Keeper): renumbered AST007 -> AST015 per the July 2026 PRN02356 amendment (fetched and confirmed in full — https://www.england.nhs.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/prn02356-quality-outcomes-framework-guidance-2026-27-july-update.pdf, pp.42-43 and changelog table p.1). Pure ID rename — wording, 20pts and 45-70% thresholds are byte-for-byte unchanged; the internal rule id (qof-ast007) is kept so overrides/dismissals keyed on it are not disturbed, only indicatorCode changed. Was HELD since 2026-08-17 pending this confirmation (see the-keeper-report-2026-08-18.md / docs/keeper/KEEPER-GAP-ANALYSIS-2026-08-22.md) — now applied. Threshold tightened for 26/27 from 50-75 to 45-70 (unchanged by this rename). The full QOF rule requires the review to include FOUR components: (1) assessment of asthma control, (2) recording of number of exacerbations, (3) assessment of inhaler technique, (4) written personalised action plan. Sentinel cannot verify all four components are present; presence of an asthma-review code is the closest approximation. Clinician must verify the written action plan and other elements. 2026-08-28: added treatNeverRecordedAsOverdue — a long-standing asthma-register patient with NO review EVER recorded now shows overdue (red), not neutral no_data, matching the AST014 fix (a genuine miss should never render as ambiguous absence of data). Only applies once the register-coded date itself is outside the current window; a recently-registered patient with no review yet still correctly shows no_data.

rules.indicatorName: Objective test within 3 months of new asthma diagnosis (post-Apr 2025)
rules.source: QOF 26/27 AST014 (PRN02356 July 2026 update, p.42: "AST014. The percentage of patients with a new diagnosis of asthma on or after 1 April 2025 with a record of an objective test between 3 months before or 3 months after diagnosis." 15pts, 45-80%)
rules.notes: 2026-08-28 (The Keeper): renumbered AST012 -> AST014 per the July 2026 PRN02356 amendment (fetched and confirmed in full — https://www.england.nhs.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/prn02356-quality-outcomes-framework-guidance-2026-27-july-update.pdf, pp.42-43 and changelog table p.1: "AST014 Changed indicator ID due to asthma register change", thresholds/points unchanged). Pure ID rename — wording, 15pts and 45-80% thresholds are byte-for-byte unchanged from prior AST012; the internal rule id (qof-ast012) is kept so overrides/dismissals keyed on it are not disturbed, only indicatorCode changed. Was HELD since 2026-08-17 pending this confirmation (see the-keeper-report-2026-08-18.md / docs/keeper/KEEPER-GAP-ANALYSIS-2026-08-22.md) — now applied. Applies to patients newly diagnosed with asthma on or after 1 April 2025, with an objective test (spirometry with BDR, FeNO, or peak flow variability) within 3 months either side of diagnosis. 2026-08-27: gated on requiresRegisterCodedFrom (2025-04-01) — the asthma register problem's codedDate is used as a proxy for diagnosis date, so patients coded before that date (or with no coded date) no longer raise this chip at all. Sentinel still cannot verify the exact 3-month window around diagnosis, only that an objective test was recorded in the last year for a patient diagnosed on/after 1 Apr 2025 — useful as a prompt, not a claim verifier.

rules.indicatorName: COPD review in preceding 12 months with MRC dyspnoea
rules.notes: Includes record of number of exacerbations and MRC dyspnoea scale. Encounter-coded; relies on Sentinel's journal endpoint fetch.

rules.indicatorName: Falling eGFR trend
rules.notes: Clinical-review trend monitor, not a QOF claim indicator. Observation history is required: where only the latest eGFR is available the chip shows no_data until multi-point history exists. NICE NG203 defines accelerated CKD progression as a sustained decrease in eGFR of >=15 mL/min/1.73m2 within 12 months (or >=25% with a change in GFR category). Window is 24 months to capture enough GP data points (annual bloods mean 12 months yields only 1-2 readings). Confirm a sustained fall on repeat testing and exclude AKI before acting.

rules.indicatorName: Raised potassium (hyperkalaemia)
rules.source: NICE CKS Hyperkalaemia / UK Kidney Association (2020)
rules.notes: Hyperkalaemia clinical-safety alert. AMBER 5.5-5.9 mmol/L (mild): first exclude pseudohyperkalaemia (haemolysed or delayed sample) and recheck; review contributing drugs (ACEi/ARB, MRA/spironolactone, potassium-sparing diuretics, NSAIDs, trimethoprim, potassium supplements) and dietary potassium. RED >=6.0 mmol/L (moderate to severe): arrange urgent same-day clinical assessment and a 12-lead ECG. K+ >=6.5 mmol/L, or any ECG changes (peaked T waves, broadened QRS), is a medical emergency - give IV calcium gluconate for cardioprotection, insulin-glucose +/- salbutamol, continuous ECG monitoring and urgent senior/renal input. Always identify and treat the underlying cause.

rules.indicatorName: Rising HbA1c trend (diabetes)
rules.source: NICE NG28 (type 2 diabetes in adults) / NICE NG17 (type 1 diabetes)
rules.notes: Clinical-review trend monitor for worsening glycaemic control in people on the diabetes register (fires only when the patient is on the DM register). Not a QOF claim indicator. Values are in mmol/mol (IFCC units). Multi-point HbA1c history is required: where only the latest result is available the chip shows no_data until history exists. Window is 24 months to capture enough readings (HbA1c is typically checked 3-6 monthly in diabetes). The >=10 mmol/mol rise is a pragmatic review threshold, not a fixed guideline cut-off - adjust to local policy. A sustained rise suggests deteriorating control: review adherence, diet/lifestyle, intercurrent illness or steroids, and consider treatment intensification per NICE NG28/NG17. Confirm on repeat testing and interpret alongside the individualised HbA1c target (commonly 48 mmol/mol, or 53 mmol/mol where treatment carries hypoglycaemia risk).

rules.indicatorName: Offer of referral to a weight-management programme in obesity
rules.source: QOF 26/27 OB004 (NHS England PRN02356): "The percentage of patients aged 18 or over living with obesity... who have been referred to a weight management programme within 90 days of the BMI being recorded." 5pts, 10-30%. CONFIRMED 2026-08-28 (The Keeper) by fetching the primary guidance in full — https://www.england.nhs.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/prn02356-quality-outcomes-framework-guidance-2026-27-july-update.pdf p.70 (indicator wording) and p.12 (Table of indicator changes: "New indicator – 10-30%" / "New – 5 pts") — both match the previously-corroborated values exactly. Numerator cluster confirmed 2026-08-28 against the official QOF v51 business rules (Obesity_v51.3, https://digital.nhs.uk/data-and-information/data-collections-and-data-sets/data-collections/quality-and-outcomes-framework-qof/business-rules/quality-and-outcomes-framework-qof-business-rules-v51-2026): cluster WTMGREF_COD "Weight management programme referral codes" (SNOMED refset 999037041000230107) — a single general referral cluster, not split by tier, so the existing tier-2/tier-3-worded match terms are a reasonable free-text approximation of it, not an under-match.
rules.notes: ENABLED 2026-08-28 (The Keeper) — was shipped disabled pending CSO confirmation of points/thresholds; that confirmation is now done (see source) so the stated blocker is resolved. The true definition requires the referral to be offered within 90 days of the qualifying BMI being recorded — Sentinel cannot verify that 90-day timing, so this observation-recent approximation checks only for a weight-management-referral code within the QOF year (a genuine, documented approximation limit, not a reason to keep it disabled). Depends on the OB register, which is itself a BMI-driven approximation. UNMODELLED PCA exception clusters exist in the official ruleset (WTMGREFDEC_COD — patient declined referral; WTMGSU_COD — service unavailable; WTMGPU_COD — programme unsuitable for the patient): a patient with a coded decline/unavailability/unsuitability entry is a legitimate QOF exception, not a missed referral, but Sentinel has no personalised-care-adjustment concept and cannot suppress the chip for them — same class of limitation already documented elsewhere in this file for other PCA-bearing indicators. Sentinel's substring matching cannot consume SNOMED refset IDs directly (see the file's own top-level notes); this citation exists for source-accuracy and for anyone with NHS TRUD access wanting to pull the actual member-code text to refine the match list further.

rules.source: PCIT OB005 (https://support.primarycareit.co.uk/portal/en-gb/kb/articles/ob005#What_makes_a_patient_eligible) + QOF 26/27 PRN02356 13pts/50-80%. Denominator is OBES2_REG (TA1026 funding-variation cohort). Numerator is three pathway codes in the contract year (WTMGPHARM_COD / WTMGBSPREF_COD / SHARDECMAK_COD), not drug brand names. Rewritten 2026-09-05 to match PCIT eligibility/achievement/removals.
rules.notes: MATCHES PCIT OB005 as of 2026-09-05: denominator is qof-reg-obes2 (age ≥18, BMI ≥35 or ≥32.5 with coded adjusted ethnicity, ≥4 of 5 comorbidities) — not the general OB register. Achievement is the three NHS obesity-pathway codes (plus 6+6 carry-over if not achieved last year). Drug brand names (orlistat / GLP-1s) no longer count as achievement; a tirzepatide/Mounjaro script without WTMGPHARM_COD removes eligibility (T2DM use). PCAs implemented: ever bariatric surgery; listed unsuitable/declined/unavailable/contraindication codes; invited twice ≥7 days apart; late BMI in last 90 days of year without prior-year PCA; new registration in last 3 months of year when registeredDate is known. Achievement overrides PCAs. Residual limits: ethnicity unknown uses BMI ≥35; dyslipidaemia lipids use latest result not an in-year diagnosis code; ASCVD/OSA/HTN/T2DM are substring approximations of TRUD clusters; several PCA clusters have no published SNOMED members yet (placeholders wired by text); not a QOF claim tool.

rules.indicatorName: Dementia care plan review in preceding 12 months
rules.source: QOF 26/27 DEM004 — PRN02356 (NHS England). CORRECTED 2026-07-25 (The Keeper, qof-001 RED): previous encoding at 30pts/60-90% was wrong (primary PDF was 403 on 2026-07-11 run; incorrect values were used). Correct values 14pts/35-70% confirmed at HIGH confidence from multiple independent QOF 2026/27 guidance sources (PracticeIndex, QMasters, Primary Care IT) all citing PRN02356 directly. VERIFIER-B confirmed at HIGH confidence.
rules.notes: Dementia care plan review in the preceding 12 months. The full QOF requirement includes review of: current symptoms, medications (especially anticholinergic burden), carer needs, and advance care planning status. Sentinel approximates with presence of a dementia-review or care-plan code within the year — it cannot verify that all review components were addressed. Clinician must confirm full review including carer assessment. Frailty exclusion is NOT applied here per PRN02356 (dementia is itself a frailty condition — the review is the intervention, not a treatment target).

rules.indicatorName: BP <=140/90 in CKD (no frailty)
rules.source: NICE NG203 (CKD BP target). NOT a QOF 26/27 indicator — 2026-08-28 (The Keeper) fetched and read the full current NHS England QOF 2026/27 guidance (PRN02356, https://www.england.nhs.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/prn02356-quality-outcomes-framework-guidance-2026-27-july-update.pdf) end to end: CKD does not appear as a QOF clinical domain, there is no CKD register/indicator chapter, and no CKD002 exists anywhere in the document. The prior 2026-07-11 entry ("QOF 26/27 CKD002") was added on a 403'd primary source and never independently confirmed — that framing was wrong and is corrected here. Relabelled from indicatorCode CKD002 (a real-looking but non-existent QOF code — risked a clinician mistaking this for something that counts toward practice QOF income/reporting) to CKD-BP and recategorised as a non-QOF safety-monitoring prompt, matching the existing trend-egfr-falling/K-HIGH/trend-hba1c-rising pattern in this file. The underlying clinical check (BP control in CKD) remains genuinely useful per NICE NG203 and is kept firing unchanged — only the false QOF-indicator framing is removed. rule id (qof-ckd002) and check logic are unchanged so no override/dismissal breaks.
rules.notes: CKD blood-pressure control prompt, NOT a QOF-scored indicator (see source). Target ≤140/90 per NICE NG203; in CKD patients with ACR >70 mg/mmol (proteinuria) the NICE NG203 target is tighter (≤130/80) — this rule enforces the more general 140/90 threshold only. Frailty exclusion retained. Note the NICE NG136 (hypertension) BP monitoring is a separate activity; this rule applies to CKD register patients regardless of whether they are also on the HYP register.

rules.indicatorName: ACE-I or ARB in CKD with hypertension and proteinuria
rules.source: NICE NG203 (RAS-inhibition in proteinuric CKD). NOT a QOF 26/27 indicator — same 2026-08-28 (The Keeper) full-document confirmation as CKD-BP (qof-ckd002): CKD has no QOF clinical domain, register or indicator chapter in the current guidance and no CKD003 exists anywhere in it. The prior 2026-07-11 entry ("QOF 26/27 CKD003") was added on a 403'd primary source and never independently confirmed — corrected here. Relabelled from indicatorCode CKD003 to CKD-RASI and recategorised as a non-QOF safety-monitoring prompt (same pattern as CKD-BP). The underlying clinical check (ACEi/ARB in proteinuric hypertensive CKD) remains genuinely useful per NICE NG203 and is kept firing unchanged — only the false QOF-indicator framing is removed. rule id (qof-ckd003) and check logic are unchanged so no override/dismissal breaks.
rules.notes: ACE inhibitor or ARB prompt for CKD patients with hypertension and proteinuria (ACR>70 mg/mmol or equivalent) — NOT a QOF-scored indicator (see source). Sentinel approximates by checking ACE-I/ARB presence in CKD patients with any coded hypertension (requiresAnyProblem is negation-aware; 'family history of hypertension' does not qualify). This will over-flag CKD+HYP patients without significant proteinuria — clinician must verify ACR status. A full ACR-observation-threshold gate would need an engine extension.
